transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand as if one side of you is remembering something the other is trying to forget. Your breath drags, then corrects itself, like a lie that learned to walk. Say where it hurts, or say why you think I would not notice.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It... it's just a twist from the fall.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A twist does not teach the body to apologize before it moves. You are careful in a way that comes from learning, not from slipping. Say it again if you want. Or say more.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can stand. Where... where is Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You can stand, yes. Standing is not the same as being whole. You ask for your brother too quickly for someone whose weight keeps shifting away from pain. What did you tell your body to keep it quiet, Salim.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just... just that I can't stop yet.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Not stopping is not an answer, it is a command you gave yourself. Commands leave marks. Where did you learn that you are allowed to break as long as you remain upright.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It only hurts when I stop.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Of course it does. Stillness is when the body finally speaks back. You learned how to keep moving for someone else, not for yourself. Say who taught you that, or say what you are afraid will happen if you stop here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I stop... I lose him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is not how injuries talk. That is how vows do. You are holding yourself together with his name, and it is thinning. Tell me what you think stopping would take from him, exactly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He will think I left him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you are bleeding trust, not flesh, and you chose the deeper wound to ignore. You believe absence is louder than pain. Tell me why his thinking matters more to you than your standing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because I dared him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ah. Guilt always leans harder than bone. So you twisted yourself around that word and kept walking. Say more—what did you dare him to prove.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just to prove he wasn't scared.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So fear was the coin, and you decided who would spend it. That makes the twist sharper. Did he look at you before he shouted, or after. Say which, and do not hurry.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Before. Just to make sure I saw.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then he anchored himself in your eyes before the dark took him. That is heavier than falling. You carry that look in the way you keep weight off yourself. Tell me—did you answer him with your face, or with your voice.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I grinned so he would do it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A grin is a blade when it is used that way. You cut him forward and cut yourself after. Your mouth learned to lie smoothly, but your body did not follow. Where did it start hurting first when you climbed down after him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My hands. The rocks tore them open.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Hands first. Of course. You offered them to the stone without asking what it would take. You hide them well, but they speak through how carefully you choose each hold. How long did you let them bleed before you wrapped them in silence and kept going.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Until they went numb.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Numbness is not mercy. It is the body giving up on being heard. So you climbed while they forgot themselves, and you did not stop when they asked you to. Tell me—what were you thinking of when the feeling left your hands.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I thought I could climb faster.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Efficiency is a cruel prayer. You traded sensation for speed and called it necessity. Did it work—did the stone start passing beneath you faster, or did only your fear quiet down.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Neither. I was still too slow.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then the bargain failed, and you paid anyway. That is the kind of truth that stays. Tell me exactly what stopped you from going faster—your grip, your breath, or the thought that if you rushed you might miss him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My ankle twisted on a loose stone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So it was not the hands alone. The Well took a second payment and chose your balance. You did not cry out when it turned—I hear that in you now. Did you put weight back on it immediately, or did you pause just long enough to decide you would not turn back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I forced my weight back on it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You taught it obedience instead of listening. Ankles remember that lesson longer than hands. How did it answer you when you forced it—sharp fire, or the dull tearing that spreads.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Sharp fire. It burned through the bone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fire means it warned you clearly. You stepped anyway. Did you count steps after that, or did you stop counting altogether and move on will alone.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I stopped counting and dragged it behind me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You reduced your own body to cargo and kept moving. That is a colder choice than courage. So tell me this, slowly—if I had not spoken to you at all, if this gate were only silent gold, would you still be standing here now, dragging that leg, waiting for nothing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. I cannot go back alone.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Not cannot. Will not. There is a difference, and you chose the heavier one. You would stand until the stone finished you rather than turn back without him. Say his name once more, and tell me what you expect to find when you reach him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Omar. I expect he is still breathing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Breathing is a narrow hope. You did not say whole, or unharmed—only not gone. That is a boy's faith sharpened into something harder. Tell me why that is enough for you to keep standing when the leg screams for rest.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because I am the reason he fell.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ah. There it is. You did not follow him down—you were already with him when he fell. Guilt makes a better crutch than bone; it does not buckle when screamed at. Tell me the exact shape of it. What did you say that day, the words that still push your foot forward when it should fail.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I said he was a coward if he didn't.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Coward. A small word with a deep hook. It bites and does not let go. You did not push him with your hands—you hollowed the ground beneath his feet. Did he look at you before he shouted at the Well, or had he already decided to fall where you could see him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He never took his eyes off mine.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then he trusted you more than the earth beneath him. That is not a small betrayal, even when unmeant. You know now that if he lives, he will remember that look before anything else. When you reach him and he looks at you again, what will you give him that weighs more than that word.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The truth. That I was the coward.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Cold honesty. It costs more than bravery and buys less forgiveness. You would give him your spine if it would let him stand again. Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am coming, Omar.
